title: Dispatch CUS 8: Two Alderwicks Sign Their Separate Registers
summary: The doorways close after both councils acknowledge the households across them.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The other Alderwick’s council adopted the limited census entry late Friday. Miss Hume and Miss Morrow signed their volumes at 9:12 yesterday morning, each certifying that the households named in the other book lie outside the jurisdiction of her own city. Neither census deletes a name or calls an inhabited street empty.

Within minutes, surveyors reported that the walls had stopped moving. The cracks above Vesper Row remained visible but did not widen. Doors along Fenwick Lane closed one by one. The opening in Mr. Keene’s bookshop was the last.

Ada Keene stood inside her hall while Mr. Keene stood among his shelves. Her daughter came to the threshold with the family photograph. Mr. Keene had brought a portrait of his wife taken before her death. They held the pictures where both could see them. Mrs. Keene then gave him a pressed violet from her garden. He placed it in a book before the door became brick.

Dr. Saye has examined both sets of remaining buildings. No person has been displaced. Elsie Hume’s wrist is healing, and Inspector Voss reports no further structural movement. The eviction notices on both sides have been cancelled by written order.

Miss Morrow says the entries will remain in Alderwick’s census with an explanation, although only one set of streets can be visited from this side. The official count of the north ward will include its own households. A supplementary schedule will preserve the names of the twenty-three across the closed boundary.
